newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF-MAT does not rule out external growth.
newsitem.headline: AGF-MAT does not rule out external growth.

text.p: AGF-MAT, created from a merger of the transport activities of insurance groups AGF and Camat, does not rule out external growth as long as it does not hit profitability, company chairman Yves Mansion said.

AGF-MAT, owned 76.6 percent by Assurances Generales de France (AGF), should post four billion francs ($792 million) in premium income and have a net profit of around "a hundred million francs", near its 1995 pro forma level, Mansion, who is also managing director of AGF, told Reuters.
Italian insurer INA holds 19.9 percent of the capital of the new company, French company Athena/PFA, part of Groupe Worms 1.3 percent and German group Nurnberger 2.2 percent.

AGF acquired Camat from INA in June. "We realise in doing this move that these are cyclical, volatile markets," Mansion said. "The years 1994 and 1995 were the height of the cycle. For 1997 and 1998, we expect a fall."
He predicted consolidation in the sector as a result of tough competition and smaller margins, saying that the end result could be just a dozen players.

He did not rule out other alliances, saying the company was open to "portfolios whose managers think they are a little too small to be truly profitable or too exposed or which do not correspond to their strategic choices".
But he said the group would not sacrifice profitability to grow. AGF-MAT is expecting a return on equity of 10 percent in 1996.
Mansion said the takeover of Camat had given AGF the size necessary to lead manage coinsurance operations.
Currently AGF-MAT has a little over 10 percent of the world market in aviation and three percent of the shipping market.
The total transport insurance market worldwide represents less than $10 billion of which some 3.5 billion are in aviation and five billion are in shipping.

Of the four billion francs in gross premium income of AGF-MAT, three billion comes from transport insurance and one billion from non-life. This activity will be transferred by the end of the year into a 100-percent-owned subsidiary of AGF-MAT, to be known as Camat-IARD.

Mansion did not rule out an eventual return to stock market listing for AGF-MAT but said it would be necessary to reduce the volatility of its earnings stemming from the cyclical nature of its business.

The current main players in transport insurance are Generali, Lloyds, American International Group Inc (AIG), Allianz, Commercial Union. In France, aside from AGF-MAT, UAP has a strong presence with Reunion Francaise.
